Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 2 y + 6 z &=2 \\ - 3 x - 6 y - 18 z &=-6 \\ 2 x + 5 y + 15 z &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 2 \\ -3 & -6 & -18 & -6 \\ 2 & 5 & 15 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 15 & 6\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-2\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2 \\ y + 3 z &=2 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-2 \\ y &=2 - 3 z \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 2 - 3 z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -5 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 2 & 4 & 10\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-1\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 4 & 10\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(1\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}- 4 x - 12 y - 28 z &=-4 \\ 5 x + 16 y + 38 z &=5 \\ 2 x + 6 y + 14 z &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-4 & -12 & -28 & -4 \\ 5 & 16 & 38 & 5 \\ 2 & 6 & 14 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{1}:=\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 7 & 1 \\ 5 & 16 & 38 & 5 \\ 2 & 6 & 14 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(-5\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 14 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-2\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(-3\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 2 z &=1 \\ y + 3 z &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2 z + 1 \\ y &=- 3 z \\ z &=z\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $z$ is an arbitrary real number. In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 z + 1 \\ - 3 z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty )

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & 6 \\ -3 & 5 & 14 & -10 \\ 3 & -9 & -18 & 18\end{array}\right]
$$

First reduce the matrix to row echelon form, making each pivot equal to $1$.

$$
R_{2}:=R_{2}+\left(3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & 8 \\ 3 & -9 & -18 & 18\end{array}\right]
$$

R_{3}:=R_{3}+\left(-3\right)R_{1}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & -4 & -4 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$



$$
R_{2}:=\left(- \frac{1}{4}\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & -6 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only.

$$
R_{1}:=R_{1}+\left(3\right)R_{2}\qquad M\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - 3 z &=0 \\ y + z &=-2 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

The final equation is $0=0$, so it imposes no restriction. The basic variables are $x$ and $y$, and the free variable is $z$. Find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z$. Therefore, the general solution is

$$
